## Summary

**Search process:**
- Declared three stopping rules upfront (`best_so_far_above` 1.2 → stop, `failures_at_least` 3 → stop, `last_gain_at_most` 0.02 → restart), and a weak prior on feature 0 (long) before any data-dependent moves.
- `init` anchored on feature 32 (Sharpe 0.385); `extend_best` found [32+, 35-] at 0.483.
- A further extend to 3 features degraded performance, triggering my restart rule. I then explored 6 more anchors (33, 18, 16, 19, 38, and 38+32) via repeated restart/extend cycles.
- Across all branches, **[33+, 35-]** consistently emerged as the strongest rule, at **Sharpe 0.491 (all-years-equal) / 0.554 (recent-weighted)** — clearly ahead of every other branch tried (which ranged 0.14–0.46) and well above the baseline model (0.183 / 0.246).
- Given this convergent evidence across 7 distinct anchors, I adjusted my failure-threshold trigger (logged as a change) to formally stop the search rather than continue churning on low-value restarts.

**Submission:** I submitted the rule **[33+, 35-]** as my candidate.

**Key caution:** The gate's 90% lower bound came back at **-0.625** — a wide band signaling real overfitting/selection risk from the search (7+ anchors tried). I did not take the in-sample Sharpe at face value.

**Prediction:** mean net Sharpe **0.20**, sd **0.40** out-of-sample — a substantial haircut from the in-sample ~0.49–0.55, reflecting selection-effect inflation, the wide gate bound, and the fact that this is only a 2-feature rule (modest diversification).
